chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim the interpreter, known as Abi al-Hasan al-Jurjani, may God be pleased with him, narrated to me: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father Zayn al-'Abidin Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon them.

That the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) stood up when Ja'far ibn Abi Talib came to him from Abyssinia, and he faced him with twelve steps, embraced him, kissed what was between his eyes, and wept, and said: 'I do not know which makes me more joyful: your arrival, O Ja'far, or God's opening [victory] for your brother at Khaybar?' And he wept for joy at seeing him.

key_terms.اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ خُطْوَة: Twelve steps, a specific gesture of honor and welcome
key_terms.الْحَبَشَة: Abyssinia (modern-day Ethiopia), the place of exile for early Muslims
key_terms.خَيْبَر: Khaybar, a fortress city where a significant victory occurred around the time of Ja'far's return
key_terms.مَا بَيْنَ الْعَيْنَيْنِ: The area between the eyes (forehead), a common place for kissing as a sign of affection

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad welcome Ja'far ibn Abi Talib upon his return from Abyssinia?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this chain of transmission to highlight the profound emotional bond between the Prophet and Ja'far, known as 'Dhu al-Yadayn' (Possessor of Two Hands) for his distinct physical features. The Prophet’s tears of joy at the convergence of Ja'far's safe return and the conquest of Khaybar underscore the significance of the Banu Hashim's resilience and the divine favor bestowed upon the Ahl al-Bayt. This event is often cited in Shia scholarship to illustrate the spiritual and emotional centrality of the Imams within the prophetic household.
